vocabulary.title: Q1 - What do you do?
idioms: Teaching is the profession that teaches all other professions - "O'qituvchilik - barcha kasblarni o'rgatuvchi kasb"
sentenceStarters: "I'm currently working as..." - "Men hozirda ... bo'lib ishlayman"
"My job primarily involves..." - "Mening ishim asosan ... ni o'z ichiga oladi"
"I've been in this profession for..." - "Men bu kasbda ... yildan beri ishlayman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'm currently working as an English language teacher at a private language center in Tashkent. I've been in this profession for about three years now.
My job primarily involves teaching English to students of various levels, from beginners to advanced learners. I also prepare students for international exams like IELTS and CEFR.
It's a genuinely rewarding career because I get to see my students make progress and achieve their goals. As they say, "Teaching is the profession that teaches all other professions".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men hozirda Toshkentdagi xususiy til markazida ingliz tili o'qituvchisi bo'lib ishlayman. Taxminan uch yildan beri shu kasb bilan shug'ullanib kelayapman.

Mening ishim asosan turli darajadagi, boshlang'ichdan tortib to ilg'or o'quvchilargacha bo'lgan talabalarga ingliz tilidan dars berishni o'z ichiga oladi. Men shuningdek talabalarni IELTS va CEFR kabi xalqaro imtihonlarga tayyorlayman.

Bu chinakamiga qoniqarli kasb, chunki men o'quvchilarimning o'sishini va maqsadlariga erishayotganini ko'raman. Aytishlaricha, "O'qituvchilik - bu boshqa barcha kasblarga o'rgatadigan kasbdir".

questions.prompt: What is the most important part of your job?
questions.sampleA2: I work in shop. The most important is talk to customers. I help them find things and they are happy. And I like to talk.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think the most important part of my job is probably making sure everything runs smoothly. For example, if the computers aren't working, nobody can do their work. So, I have to fix them. It's sometimes stressful, but also satisfying when I solve a problem.
questions.sampleB2: The thing is, I'd say the most important part of my job is problem-solving. When something goes wrong with a campaign, I have to think on my feet and come up with a fix quickly. On top of that, keeping my colleagues in the loop really matters, otherwise small issues can snowball into big ones.
questions.uzSampleA1: Mening ishim... muhim... odamlarga yordam berish. Xursandman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men do'konda ishlayman. Eng muhimi, mijozlar bilan gaplashish. Men ularga narsalarni topishga yordam beraman va ular xursand bo'lishadi. Va men gaplashishni yaxshi ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, menimcha, ishimning eng muhim qismi, ehtimol, hamma narsaning muammosiz ishlashini ta'minlashdir. Masalan, agar kompyuterlar ishlamasa, hech kim o'z ishini qila olmaydi. Shuning uchun men ularni tuzatishim kerak. Ba'zan bu stressli, lekin muammoni hal qilganimda qoniqarli ham bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Menimcha, mening ishimning eng muhim jihati muammolarni hal qilishdir. Men IT sohasida ishlayman va kundalik texnik xizmat muhim bo'lsa-da, men keltiradigan haqiqiy qadriyat murakkab texnik muammolarni aniqlash va hal qilishdan iborat. Bu ko'pincha tanqidiy fikrlashni va bizning tizimlarimizni chuqur tushunishni talab qiladi. Bundan tashqari, ushbu yechimlarni texnik bilimga ega bo'lmagan hamkasblarga samarali yetkazish, minimal uzilishlarni ta'minlash va kelajakdagi muammolarning oldini olish uchun ham juda muhimdir.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - What is the most important part of your job?
idioms: A good teacher can inspire hope and ignite the imagination - "Yaxshi o'qituvchi umid uyg'otadi va tasavvurni yoqadi"
sentenceStarters: "I believe the most important part is..." - "Men eng muhim qismi ... deb o'ylayman"
"It's crucial to..." - "... juda muhim"
"Additionally, I think..." - "Bundan tashqari, men ... deb o'ylayman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I believe the most important part of my job is building rapport with my students and creating a supportive learning environment.
When students feel comfortable and motivated, they learn much more effectively. It's crucial to understand each student's individual needs and adapt my teaching style accordingly.
Additionally, I think providing constructive feedback is essential – helping students identify their weaknesses while also acknowledging their strengths. As they say, "A good teacher can inspire hope and ignite the imagination".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Menimcha, ishimning eng muhim qismi talabalarim bilan yaxshi munosabat o'rnatish va qo'llab-quvvatlovchi o'quv muhitini yaratishdir.

Talabalar o'zlarini qulay va rag'batlantirilgan his qilganda, ular ancha samaraliroq o'rganadilar. Har bir talabaning individual ehtiyojlarini tushunish va shunga mos ravishda o'qitish uslubimni moslashtirish juda muhim.

Bundan tashqari, menimcha, konstruktiv fikr-mulohazalarni taqdim etish muhimdir – talabalarga o'zlarining zaif tomonlarini aniqlashga yordam berish, shu bilan birga ularning kuchli tomonlarini ham e'tirof etish. Aytishlaricha, "Yaxshi o'qituvchi umid bag'ishlay oladi va tasavvurni uyg'ota oladi".

questions.prompt: Do you work with other people or alone?
questions.sampleA2:
I work with people and alone.

I like to work with people because it is fun.

But sometimes I work alone because it is quiet.
questions.sampleB1:
I usually work with other people.

I think it's better because we can share ideas.

For example, we often discuss problems together and find solutions.

However, sometimes I need to work alone to concentrate on my tasks.
questions.sampleB2: I suppose it's a bit of both, really. Most of the time I work alongside my teammates — we bounce ideas off each other and tackle projects together. That said, when I need to knuckle down and focus, I'll shut myself away for a couple of hours. Honestly, that mix suits me down to the ground.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men odamlar bilan ham, yolg'iz ham ishlayman.

Odamlar bilan ishlashni yaxshi ko'raman, chunki bu qiziqarli.

Lekin ba'zida yolg'iz ishlayman, chunki u yerda tinch.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men odatda boshqa odamlar bilan ishlayman.

Menimcha, bu yaxshiroq, chunki biz fikrlarimizni baham ko'rishimiz mumkin.

Masalan, biz ko'pincha muammolarni birgalikda muhokama qilamiz va yechimlar topamiz.

Biroq, ba'zida vazifalarimga diqqatni jamlash uchun yolg'iz ishlashim kerak.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men asosan boshqa odamlar bilan ishlayman, garchi ishimning yakka tartibda ishlashni talab qiladigan elementlari ham mavjud.

Ko'plab loyihalarim uchun hamkorlik muhim, chunki turli jamoa a'zolari o'ziga xos nuqtai nazarlar va ko'nikmalarni olib kelishadi.

Biz ko'pincha birgalikda fikr yuritamiz va muammolarni hal qilamiz, bu esa yanada innovatsion natijalarga olib keladi.

Shunga qaramay, men mustaqil ishlashga sarflagan vaqtimni ham qadrlayman, chunki bu menga chuqur e'tibor qaratishga va chalg'ituvchi omillarsiz vazifalarni samarali bajarishga imkon beradi.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you work with other people or alone?
idioms: Two heads are better than one - "Ikki bosh bitta boshdan yaxshi"
sentenceStarters: "In my job, I work in both settings..." - "Ishimda men ikkala sharoitda ham ishlayman..."
"During classes, I'm constantly..." - "Darslar davomida men doimo..."
"However, some tasks I typically do alone..." - "Biroq, ba'zi ishlarni men odatda yolg'iz qilaman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
In my job, I work in both settings, but predominantly with other people.
During classes, I'm constantly interacting with students, which requires strong interpersonal skills. I also collaborate with my colleagues to share teaching materials and discuss effective methodologies.
However, lesson planning and grading are tasks I typically do alone, which allows me to focus and be more productive. I actually enjoy this balance – as they say, "Two heads are better than one", but sometimes you need solitude to think creatively.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening ishimda men ikkala sharoitda ham ishlayman, lekin asosan boshqa odamlar bilan.

Darslar davomida men doimiy ravishda talabalar bilan muloqotda bo'laman, bu esa kuchli shaxslararo ko'nikmalarni talab qiladi. Men shuningdek, o'quv materiallarini baham ko'rish va samarali metodologiyalarni muhokama qilish uchun hamkasblarim bilan hamkorlik qilaman.

Biroq, dars rejalashtirish va baholash men odatda yolg'iz bajaradigan vazifalar bo'lib, bu menga diqqatni jamlash va unumliroq bo'lish imkonini beradi. Menga bu muvozanat juda yoqadi – aytishlaricha, "Bir bosh yaxshi, ikkisi undan ham yaxshi", lekin ba'zida ijodiy fikrlash uchun xilvat kerak bo'ladi.

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1:
I see a man. He is on a sofa.

I see people. They play hockey.
questions.sampleA2:
I see a man on a sofa. He is drinking something.

And I see people playing hockey. They are outside and it is cold, I think.
questions.sampleB1:
In the first picture, I see a man sitting on a sofa. He looks relaxed and is probably drinking coffee.

The second picture shows people playing hockey. They are outside, and it looks like they are having fun. I think it's a winter sport.
questions.sampleB2:
These two pictures present contrasting scenes of leisure. In the first image, a man is kicking back in a modern armchair, holding a glass and reading a book or tablet. He appears to be relaxing indoors, presumably enjoying a quiet, solitary moment in a bright, minimalist setting.

By contrast, the second picture is full of energy, showing a group of adults and children having a blast playing ice hockey outdoors. They are all actively engaged in the game, bundled up against the cold. This image captures a moment of shared activity and fun, highlighting social interaction and physical exercise, which is miles apart from the calm of the first scene.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Men bir erkakni ko'ryapman. U divanda o'tiribdi.

Men odamlarni ko'ryapman. Ular xokkey o'ynashyapti.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men divanda bir odamni ko'ryapman. U nimadir ichyapti.

Va men xokkey o'ynayotgan odamlarni ko'ryapman. Ular tashqarida va menimcha, sovuq.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Birinchi rasmda divanda o'tirgan odamni ko'ryapman. U xotirjam ko'rinadi va ehtimol kofe ichyapti.

Ikkinchi rasmda xokkey o'ynayotgan odamlarni ko'rsatilgan. Ular tashqarida va ular xursandchilik qilayotganga o'xshaydi. Menimcha, bu qishki sport turi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Birinchi rasmda yolg'izlikdan zavqlanayotgan odam tasvirlangan. U divanda, xotirjam va ehtimol, issiq ichimlikdan bahramand bo'layotganga o'xshaydi.

Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda tashqarida xokkey o'ynayotgan bir guruh odamlar ko'rsatilgan. Ular juda ijtimoiy va faol vaqt o'tkazayotganga o'xshaydi.

Rasmlar odamlarning bo'sh vaqtlarini o'tkazishning turli usullarini ta'kidlaydi; biri sokin va ichki, boshqasi esa g'ayratli va jamoaviy.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: the more the merrier - "qancha ko'p bo'lsa, shuncha qiziq"
sentenceStarters: "These pictures show contrasting ways of..." - "Bu rasmlar ... ning qarama-qarshi usullarini ko'rsatadi"
"In the first picture, I can see..." - "Birinchi rasmda men ... ko'ryapman"
"The second picture shows a completely different scene..." - "Ikkinchi rasm butunlay boshqacha manzarani ko'rsatadi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
These two pictures show contrasting ways of spending time – alone versus with others.
In the first picture, I can see a young man relaxing alone on a comfortable couch. He's holding a cup, probably coffee, and appears to be enjoying some quiet time by himself. The setting looks like a modern, cozy living room with natural light coming through the window.
The second picture shows a completely different scene – a group of friends playing hockey outdoors in winter. They look like they're having a great time together, laughing and being actively engaged in the game. It's a social activity that brings people together.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki rasm vaqtni o'tkazishning qarama-qarshi usullarini ko'rsatadi – yolg'izlik va boshqalar bilan birgalikda.

Birinchi rasmda men yosh yigitni qulay divanda yolg'iz dam olayotganini ko'raman. U qo'lida bir chashka ushlab turibdi, ehtimol qahva, va o'zi bilan sokin vaqtdan zavqlanayotganga o'xshaydi. Muhit zamonaviy, shinam yashash xonasiga o'xshaydi, derazadan tabiiy yorug'lik tushib turibdi.

Ikkinchi rasm butunlay boshqa manzarani ko'rsatadi – bir guruh do'stlar qishda tashqarida xokkey o'ynashmoqda. Ular birgalikda juda yaxshi vaqt o'tkazayotganga o'xshaydi, kulishadi va o'yinga faol ishtirok etishadi. Bu odamlarni birlashtiradigan ijtimoiy faoliyat.

questions.prompt: Would you prefer to stay alone or with other people?
questions.sampleA2:
I like to stay alone.

Because it is quiet.

And I can relax.

But I also like to see my friends.
questions.sampleB1:
Well, I think it depends.

Sometimes I prefer to be alone, because I need time to relax.

For example, after a long day at work, I like to read a book in peace.

However, I also enjoy being with other people.

It's fun to go out with friends and have a good time.
questions.sampleB2: Honestly, it depends on my mood, but on the whole I lean towards being around other people. I'm quite a sociable person, so I get a real buzz out of chatting and doing things with friends. That said, every now and then I do need a bit of time to myself to recharge my batteries and unwind.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men yolg'iz qolishni yoqtiraman.

Chunki u yerda tinch.

Va men dam olishim mumkin.

Lekin do'stlarimni ko'rishni ham yoqtiraman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, bu vaziyatga bog'liq.

Ba'zan yolg'iz bo'lishni afzal ko'raman, chunki dam olish uchun vaqt kerak.

Masalan, ishda uzoq kundan so'ng, tinchlikda kitob o'qishni yaxshi ko'raman.

Biroq, men boshqa odamlar bilan birga bo'lishdan ham zavqlanaman.

Do'stlar bilan ko'chaga chiqib, yaxshi vaqt o'tkazish juda qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Bu murakkab savol, chunki ikkala variant ham o'ziga xos jozibaga ega.

Bir tomondan, men yolg'izlikni juda qadrlayman.

O'zimga vaqt ajratish menga stressdan xalos bo'lishga va sevimli mashg'ulotlarim bilan hech kim xalaqit bermasdan shug'ullanishga imkon beradi.

Boshqa tomondan, insoniy aloqa farovonlik uchun juda muhim.

Tajribalarni baham ko'rish va boshqalar bilan mazmunli suhbatlar qilish juda foydali.

Oxir oqibat, menimcha, ideal vaziyat ikkalasi o'rtasida muvozanatni o'z ichiga oladi; tinchlikdagi izolyatsiya lahzalari bilan almashinadigan ijtimoiy aloqa davrlari.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - Would you prefer to stay alone or with other people?
idioms: absence makes the heart grow fonder - "ayriliq sevgini kuchaytiradi"
sentenceStarters: "This really depends on the situation..." - "Bu haqiqatan ham vaziyatga bog'liq..."
"There are times when I desperately need..." - "Ba'zan menga juda kerak bo'ladi..."
"However, I'm also quite sociable..." - "Biroq, men ham juda ijtimoiyman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
This really depends on the situation and my mood, but I'd say I generally prefer a healthy balance of both.
There are times when I desperately need some alone time to recharge. After a busy week of work, I enjoy curling up with a good book or simply relaxing at home, much like the man in the first picture. Solitude gives me the space to reflect on things and clear my mind.
However, I'm also quite sociable and love spending time with friends and family. Activities like the hockey game in the second picture are incredibly fun and help strengthen relationships. Shared experiences create lasting memories.
As they say, "Everything in moderation" – too much of either can become tiresome.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu haqiqatan ham vaziyatga va kayfiyatimga bog'liq, lekin men odatda ikkalasining ham sog'lom muvozanatini afzal ko'raman, deb aytgan bo'lardim.

Ba'zida menga zaryad olish uchun juda zarur bo'lgan yolg'izlik kerak bo'ladi. Ish bilan band bo'lgan bir haftadan so'ng, men yaxshi kitob bilan o'ralashib yoki shunchaki uyda dam olishni yoqtiraman, xuddi birinchi rasmdagi odamga o'xshab. Yolg'izlik menga narsalar haqida o'ylash va fikrlarimni tozalash uchun joy beradi.

Biroq, men ham juda kirishimli odamman va do'stlarim va oilam bilan vaqt o'tkazishni yaxshi ko'raman. Ikkinchi rasmdagi xokkey o'yini kabi tadbirlar juda qiziqarli va munosabatlarni mustahkamlashga yordam beradi. Birgalikdagi tajribalar unutilmas xotiralarni yaratadi.

Aytishlaricha, "Har narsada me'yor bo'lishi kerak" – ikkalasining ham haddan tashqari ko'pligi zerikarli bo'lishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Do you remember a time when you needed to cooperate with others?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I remember. School. Group project. We worked together. It was good.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I remember a time. It was at work. We needed to work together on a project. It was difficult, but we finished it. And it was good.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I remember a time when I needed to cooperate with others. It was last year at my job. We had to do a big presentation. I think it was difficult because we had different ideas. However, we talked and found a solution. In the end, it was successful.
questions.sampleB2: Yes, definitely. Last year my colleagues and I had to pull together to organise a big company event at short notice. At first we kept stepping on each other's toes, but once we divided up the tasks, things ran like clockwork. In the end, we pulled it off brilliantly, and it really brought the team closer.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Esimda. Maktab. Guruh loyihasi. Biz birga ishladik. Yaxshi bo'ldi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, bir vaqt esimda. Bu ishda bo'lgan edi. Biz bir loyihada birga ishlashimiz kerak edi. Bu qiyin edi, lekin biz uni tugatdik. Va u yaxshi bo'ldi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men boshqalar bilan hamkorlik qilishim kerak bo'lgan vaqtni eslayman. Bu o'tgan yili ishimda bo'lgan edi. Biz katta taqdimot qilishimiz kerak edi. Menimcha, bu qiyin bo'ldi, chunki bizda har xil g'oyalar bor edi.
Ammo, biz gaplashdik va yechim topdik. Oxir-oqibat, bu muvaffaqiyatli bo'ldi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Ha, hamkorlik juda muhim bo'lgan vaziyat esimda. Bu ko'ngilli loyiha davomida bo'lgan edi. Biz jamoat bog'ini qurayotgan edik. Bir nechta ko'ngillilar bor edi, ularning har biri turli xil ko'nikmalarga va tajriba darajalariga ega edi. Dastlab, hamma bilan muvofiqlashtirish qiyin edi, chunki ba'zi odamlarning bog' dizayni haqida qat'iy fikrlari bor edi.
Shunga qaramay, biz aniq aloqa kanallarini o'rnatdik va har bir insonning fikrini qadrlashga ongli ravishda harakat qildik. Hamkorlikda ishlash va murosaga kelish orqali biz jamoa uchun chiroyli va funktsional bog' yaratishga muvaffaq bo'ldik.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Do you remember a time when you needed to cooperate with others?
idioms: Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much - "Yolg'iz kam ish qilamiz; birga esa ko'p narsaga erishamiz"
many hands make light work - "qo'l ko'p bo'lsa, ish yengil"
sentenceStarters: "I vividly remember a time when..." - "Men ... vaqtni aniq eslayman"
"I was in charge of..." - "Men ... uchun mas'ul edim"
"The experience taught me..." - "Bu tajriba menga ... o'rgatdi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I vividly remember a time during my university years when cooperation was absolutely essential.
We had a major group project in our final year – we needed to organize a large-scale English language conference. There were about eight of us in the team, and each person had specific responsibilities.
I was in charge of coordinating speakers while others handled logistics, marketing, and registration. It was challenging because we had different opinions and working styles. There were moments of tension, but we learned to compromise and find common ground.
The conference was a huge success, and the experience taught me the true value of teamwork. As they say, "Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, universitet yillarimda hamkorlik mutlaqo zarur bo'lgan bir vaqtni juda yaxshi eslayman.

Oxirgi kursimizda katta guruh loyihamiz bor edi – biz katta ko'lamli ingliz tili konferensiyasini tashkil qilishimiz kerak edi. Jamoada taxminan sakkiz kishi edik va har bir kishining o'ziga xos vazifalari bor edi.

Men ma'ruzachilarni muvofiqlashtirishga mas'ul edim, boshqalar esa logistika, marketing va ro'yxatdan o'tkazish bilan shug'ullanishdi. Bu qiyin edi, chunki bizning fikrlarimiz va ishlash uslublarimiz har xil edi. Taranglik lahzalari bo'ldi, lekin biz murosaga kelishni va umumiy til topishni o'rgandik.

Konferensiya juda muvaffaqiyatli o'tdi va bu tajriba menga jamoaviy ishning haqiqiy qadrini o'rgatdi. Aytishlaricha, "Yolg'iz o'zimiz juda oz narsa qila olamiz; birgalikda esa juda ko'p narsa qila olamiz".

questions.sampleA1: I go to school. School is good. I learn things. I like my teacher.
questions.sampleA2: I like school. I learn many things. My favorite subject is math, but I also like to read books. School is important because I want a good job later.
questions.sampleB1: I think education is very important. Schools help us learn about different subjects like science and history. I like some subjects more than others. For example, I really enjoy English class, but I don't like math very much. I think school is important for my future.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so I'd like to talk a bit about education, because it's a topic that's close to my heart. To start with, on the question of whether schools should teach both arts and science, I honestly think they absolutely should. A well-rounded education gives students the best of both worlds — science sharpens their logical, analytical thinking, whereas the arts let them tap into their creative side. If you only focus on one, you end up with fairly one-sided individuals, and to be honest, the real world calls for both. Moving on to university, I reckon the most useful courses are the practical ones that actually prepare you for a career. Things like foreign languages, digital skills and public speaking can really open doors. On top of that, I'd throw in something like financial literacy, because so many graduates leave university without the faintest idea of how to manage money. As for why some students can't stand studying at school, I think it often boils down to the rigid, one-size-fits-all curriculum. When lessons feel dull and have nothing to do with real life, it's no wonder kids switch off and lose interest. Piling on endless homework and exam pressure only makes matters worse, and it can put them off learning for good. At the end of the day, I strongly believe education should light a spark in young people rather than simply cram facts into their heads. Get that balance right, and school becomes somewhere students genuinely want to be, rather than somewhere they feel forced to go.

bulletPoints: Should schools teach both arts and science?
What kinds of courses are useful for university students?
Why do some students dislike studying at school?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Arts and science in schools:
I firmly believe that schools should teach both arts and science. A well-rounded education helps students develop different types of skills. Science teaches critical thinking and problem-solving, while arts foster creativity and emotional expression. Students need exposure to both to discover their true passions and talents.
Useful courses for university students:
For university students, I think practical courses are extremely valuable. These include foreign languages, computer skills, and communication courses. Additionally, courses on financial literacy and project management can help students prepare for the real world. Soft skills training is equally important.
Why students dislike school:
Many students dislike school for various reasons. The rigid curriculum often doesn't cater to individual interests. Furthermore, excessive homework and exam pressure can make learning feel like a burden rather than a joy. Some students also struggle with uninspiring teaching methods. As they say, "Education is not the filling of a pail, but the lighting of a fire".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Maktablarda san'at va fan:

Men maktablar san'at va fanni birgalikda o'qitishi kerak, deb qat'iy ishonaman. Har tomonlama ta'lim talabalarga turli xil ko'nikmalarni rivojlantirishga yordam beradi. Fan tanqidiy fikrlash va muammolarni hal qilishni o'rgatsa, san'at ijodkorlik va hissiy ifodani rivojlantiradi. Talabalar o'zlarining haqiqiy ishtiyoqlari va iste'dodlarini kashf qilishlari uchun ikkalasidan ham bahramand bo'lishlari kerak.

Universitet talabalari uchun foydali kurslar:

Universitet talabalari uchun amaliy kurslar juda qimmatli deb o'ylayman. Bularga xorijiy tillar, kompyuter ko'nikmalari va kommunikatsiya kurslari kiradi. Bundan tashqari, moliyaviy savodxonlik va loyihalarni boshqarish bo'yicha kurslar talabalarga real hayotga tayyorlanishga yordam beradi. Yumshoq ko'nikmalarni o'rgatish ham xuddi shunday muhim.

Nima uchun talabalar maktabni yoqtirmaydi:

Ko'p talabalar turli sabablarga ko'ra maktabni yoqtirmaydi. Qat'iy o'quv dasturi ko'pincha individual qiziqishlarga mos kelmaydi. Bundan tashqari, haddan tashqari uy vazifalari va imtihon bosimi o'rganishni quvonchdan ko'ra yukdek his qilishga olib kelishi mumkin. Ba'zi talabalar ilhomlantirmaydigan o'qitish usullari bilan ham kurashadilar. Aytishlaricha, "Ta'lim - bu chelakni to'ldirish emas, balki olovni yoqishdir".

questions.prompt: Do school uniforms make school a more effective place to learn?

questions.sampleB1:
Well, I think school uniforms have both good and bad sides.

On one hand, they can make everyone look the same, so maybe there's less bullying about clothes.

Also, it's easier in the morning because you don't have to decide what to wear.

However, uniforms can be expensive for some families.

questions.sampleB2: That's a really interesting question, and I think it's one that splits people right down the middle. Let me look at both sides before I give my own take. On the one hand, supporters of school uniforms make some fair points. For a start, uniforms create a sense of belonging and put everyone on a level playing field, so students aren't judged by what they wear or how much money their parents have. They also cut down on the morning hassle of deciding what to put on, and some would argue they help keep discipline in check, and possibly reduce issues like bullying over brand-name clothes. When everyone looks the same, it's easier for kids to focus on their studies rather than on fashion. On the other hand, critics have a point too. Uniforms can be surprisingly pricey, which hits low-income families the hardest, so ironically they can widen the gap they're meant to close. What's more, forcing everyone into the same outfit can stifle self-expression, and let's face it, there's not much solid evidence that uniforms actually boost grades, so plenty of parents feel it's an added expense for very little real payoff. Weighing it all up, I'd say uniforms have their perks, but they're certainly no magic bullet. At the end of the day, what really makes a school effective isn't the clothes the students wear — it's the quality of the teaching and how engaged the pupils feel. A uniform might set the tone, but on its own it won't turn a struggling school around.

vocabulary.title: Q8 - Do school uniforms make school a more effective place to learn?
idioms: Don't judge a book by its cover - "Kitobni muqovasiga qarab baholamang"
sentenceStarters: "This is a topic that divides opinion..." - "Bu fikrlarni bo'ladigan mavzu..."
"Supporters argue that..." - "Tarafdorlar ... deb ta'kidlaydi"
"However, opponents raise valid concerns..." - "Biroq, qarshilar asosli tashvishlarni bildiradi..."

for: School uniforms can create a sense of unity and reduce distractions in the classroom.
School uniforms can foster a sense of respect and discipline.
School uniforms can help to reduce gang-related violence and other disciplinary issues in schools.
against: School uniforms are not the most effective way to improve the learning environment in schools.
School uniforms can be expensive and can create an unequal learning environment.
School uniforms can be restrictive and limit students' ability to express themselves.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a topic that divides opinion among educators, parents, and students alike. Let me present both sides of the argument.
Supporters of school uniforms argue that they can significantly improve the learning environment. Firstly, uniforms create a sense of unity and belonging among students, which can foster school pride. Secondly, they reduce peer pressure related to clothing and minimize distractions. Additionally, uniforms can help reduce gang-related issues and promote discipline.
However, opponents raise valid concerns. Uniforms can be quite expensive, particularly for low-income families, which creates inequality rather than reducing it. Moreover, uniforms can stifle students' self-expression and creativity. Research also suggests that uniforms alone don't significantly impact academic performance.
In my view, uniforms can be helpful but aren't a magic solution. As they say, "Don't judge a book by its cover" – what matters most is the quality of teaching.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu mavzu o'qituvchilar, ota-onalar va talabalar o'rtasida bir xilda fikrlarni bo'ladi.

Maktab formalarini qo'llab-quvvatlovchilar ularning ta'lim muhitini sezilarli darajada yaxshilashi mumkinligini ta'kidlaydilar. Birinchidan, formalar talabalar o'rtasida birlik va mansublik tuyg'usini yaratadi, bu esa maktab faxrini oshirishi mumkin. Ikkinchidan, ular kiyim bilan bog'liq tengdoshlar bosimini kamaytiradi va chalg'ituvchi omillarni minimallashtiradi. Bundan tashqari, formalar guruhlar bilan bog'liq muammolarni kamaytirishga va intizomni rag'batlantirishga yordam beradi.

Biroq, qarshilar asosli xavotirlarni uyg'otadilar. Formlar juda qimmat bo'lishi mumkin, ayniqsa kam daromadli oilalar uchun, bu tenglikni kamaytirish o'rniga tengsizlikni yaratadi. Bundan tashqari, formalar talabalarning o'zini ifoda etish va ijodkorligini bo'g'ishi mumkin. Tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatadiki, formalarning o'zi akademik ko'rsatkichlarga sezilarli ta'sir ko'rsatmaydi.

Mening fikrimcha, formalar foydali bo'lishi mumkin, ammo sehrli yechim emas. Aytganlaridek, "Kitobni muqovasiga qarab baholamang" - eng muhimi, o'qitish sifati.
